prompt: You have a $\$25$ budget and each game credit costs $\$4$. Using $4c \le 25$, what is the greatest number of whole credits $c$ you can buy? Give just the number.
hint: Solve the inequality first, then think about what kind of number a count of credits has to be.

hints.text: Solve the inequality first, then think about what kind of number a count of credits has to be.
Dividing both sides by $4$ gives $c \le 6.25$. You cannot buy part of a credit, so look for the largest whole number that fits.
The largest whole number not above $6.25$ is $6$, so you can buy $6$ credits.

explanation: Divide both sides of $4c \le 25$ by $4$ to get $c \le 6.25$.
Credits only come in whole numbers, so take the largest whole number that is not more than $6.25$, which is $6$.
Check: $6$ credits cost $4 \times 6 = 24$ dollars, which fits, but $7$ credits cost $28$ dollars, so the answer is $6$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Spend it out loud
steps: Count by 4s until you would pass 25: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24 — that is 6 credits for $\$24$.
A 7th credit needs $\$28$, which is more than $\$25$. Stop at 6.
